text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Minister of Transport Vilis Krishtopans announced he will consider resigning in the wake of allegations that he violated anti-corruption laws by holding posts in four companies.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele accepted the nomination of Talavs Jundzis from the Christian Democratic Party as minister of defense.

- A Riga court found Ivars Linde, a former vice-president and acting president of Latvia's Saving Bank, guilty of exceeding his mandate and losing the bank $500,000. He was sentenced to one and half a years in prison.

- The committee formed to investigate the granting of G-24 loans concluded in a first report that the economy ministry lost $4.5 million and there were many mistakes granting the loans. The committee will carry on working until September 30.
- Latvian mountaineer Ilgvars Pauls reached the peak of mount Everest on May 27.

- President Guntis Ulmanis said he will visit the eastern town of Daugavpils, where the mayor was elected in March local elections despite the fact he was banned from running under rules that prevent people who were Communist Party members after January 1991 from getting into office.
- In the first four months of 1997, the state budget had a 16 million lat surplus.
